intro: Distinguish precisely when to negate with geen (indefinite nouns) and with niet (verbs, adjectives and definite elements).

palabras.significado: no; not any; there is no

piezas.titulo: The essential contrast between niet and geen
texto: The golden rule of negation in Dutch is: use «geen» to negate nouns preceded by an indefinite article («een») or with no article at all: «Ik drink geen koffie» (I don't drink coffee), «Ik heb geen suiker» (I don't have sugar). For everything else (verbs, adjectives, adverbs, proper names or nouns with the definite article «de/het»), «niet» is always used: «De winkel is niet open» (the shop is not open), «Ik werk vandaag niet» (I don't work today).

analisis: no coffee at all; I don't drink coffee

frases.estudio: Ik heb geen suiker, maar wel melk.
frases.alumno: I don't have sugar, but I do have milk.

frases.estudio: Mijn broer is vandaag niet thuis.
frases.alumno: My brother is not at home today.

frases.estudio: Wij werken vandaag niet; we zijn vrij.
frases.alumno: Today we don't work; we have the day off.
analisis: we are free; we have the day off

pregunta.texto: When should «geen» be used instead of «niet»?

opciones.texto: To negate nouns without a definite article or that would take «een»
opciones.explicacion: It is equivalent to "no / not any" before an indefinite noun.

opciones.texto: To negate descriptive adjectives in any position
opciones.explicacion: Adjectives are always negated with «niet» («niet open», «niet mooi»).

opciones.texto: Exclusively at the end of question sentences
opciones.explicacion: The position of «geen» depends on the noun it accompanies, not on the type of sentence.

pregunta.texto: What does the person have and what do they lack?

frase.texto: Ik heb geen suiker, maar wel melk.

opciones.texto: They have no sugar, but they do have milk.
opciones.explicacion: «Geen suiker» negates the sugar and «wel melk» affirms the presence of milk in contrast.

opciones.texto: They have plenty of sugar but no milk.
They lack both sugar and milk.
opciones.explicacion: «Wel» introduces an affirmation that compensates for the previous lack.

pregunta.texto: Complete with the correct negation particle for an adjective.

opciones.explicacion: Descriptive adjectives must always be negated with «niet», never with «geen».
«Geen» only accompanies indefinite nouns, not adjectives like «open».
Although grammatical, «wel» would affirm that it is open, the opposite of the negation.

pregunta.texto: Why are they not working today according to the text?

frase.texto: Wij werken vandaag niet; we zijn vrij.

opciones.texto: Because they have the day off today.
opciones.explicacion: «We zijn vrij» means they are free from work.

opciones.texto: Because the office is closed due to a breakdown.
opciones.explicacion: It does not mention any breakdown; they are enjoying their day off.

opciones.texto: Because they have to attend a class in Utrecht.
opciones.explicacion: It does not talk about Dutch classes, but about a rest from work.

pregunta.texto: Complete the negation before the uncountable common noun «koffie».

opciones.explicacion: Before a noun without the definite article, «geen» must be used.
With an indefinite noun «niet» is not used, but «geen».
It would express a flat affirmation ("I do drink it"), the opposite of the negative intention.

piezas.explicacion: Initial adverb with verb inversion and the negative particle «geen» before the noun.
